# Fixed allocation protocol

Recorded locally before computing held-out allocations or opening their outcomes for this comparison. This is a public-data retrospective specification, without an independent timestamp, external registration, human sign-off or sealed dataset.

**Primary cohort.** Use OULAD at the end of registration day 0. Require registration by day 0 and continued enrollment through that day. Use registration timing, credits, prior attempts, education, age band, module and recorded gender. The target is eventual Withdrawn status. Train on 2013 presentations only, exclude all test learners from training and use 2014J for evaluation. Retain one registration per learner per split (earliest presentation then lexicographically first eligible module). Each test module is a pool. Other portfolio work examined OULAD withdrawals at day 60, so only the allocation analysis is new here.

**Independent transfer.** Use UCI 856 Higher Education Students Performance Evaluation, with a distinct target of grade code 0, 1 or 2 (Fail, DD or DC). Use age, sex, high-school type, scholarship and course ID as categorical predictors. Exclude study habits, current expectations and academic-performance fields. Training uses 60% by a seeded permutation (42) of sorted student IDs, rounded down. Allocate once in the remaining campus pool. This cross-sectional test assumes the five covariates were available before final grades. Fit locally on each benchmark.

**Decision payload.** Use all eligible people. Give each policy identical probabilities, group membership, tie order and capacity. Fit fixed regularized logistic regression (C=1, standardized numeric and one-hot categorical inputs) and 40 learner bootstrap refits, seed 314. Rank within groups by the full training fit, ties by lexical student ID. The protected category is recorded female. Select floor(10% of each pool), minimum one. Compute FA*IR binomial prefix minima with a per-list null crossing bound of 0.10, finding the largest feasible quantile level by 32 bisection steps and exact Bernoulli path recursion. Enforce the identical table for every constrained method. Keep labels outside allocation inputs. Save a decision digest before scoring.

**Comparators.** Unrestricted top-k supplies the shared score ceiling. FA*IR greedily enforces prefix minima. Largest-remainder quota rounds the pool share to seats (half to female), with compliant within-set ordering. Exhaustively optimized standard group thresholds choose the feasible split maximizing the smaller group expected recall under the full fit. A position-discounted dynamic program for the two-group special case of Celis, Straszak and Vishnoi maximizes summed risk/log2(rank+1) under the same prefix bounds. The candidate is the analogous threshold allocation maximizing the tenth percentile of the 40 bootstrap worst-group expected recalls, with fixed within-group ordering. For both threshold policies retain only splits costing at most 0.01 expected captures per seat below the best feasible point-score utility. Break ties by higher total point utility then fewer female seats. Reorder selected sets by FA*IR under the common table. Optimizing the bootstrap objective by standard group thresholds can represent the candidate exactly. This tests the value of objective choice, and cannot establish a new selection mechanism.

**Endpoints and win rule.** Pool counts across modules within each benchmark. Primary utility is the smaller of female and male recall for retrospective cases. A win requires strictly positive paired 95% lower bounds against each constrained comparator on both benchmarks, plus precision no more than one percentage point below unrestricted top-k (paired lower bound at least -0.01 on each benchmark), and observed binding on each benchmark. Treat undefined group recall as insufficient evidence. Report score-utility ceiling separately from realized unrestricted captures and the hindsight label oracle min(k, cases) in each pool. Report group denominators, captures, capacity, prefix violations and membership changes. Use 5,000 paired learner bootstrap draws within pools, seed 1701, conditioning on fitted policies and saved decisions. Omit undefined draws and report counts. An intersection of wins is required, with no selection of favorable contrasts. Intervals are conditional descriptive approximations, especially on the small transfer sample. No causal intervention estimand, observed staff budget or claim of a universal strongest algorithm.
